Sulo: Privacy Policy

Last updated: 21 November 2026

Sulo is an unofficial academic companion for Universitas Hasanuddin students, as a browser extension (Chrome and Edge) and an Android app. Sulo is not an official Unhas app, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Universitas Hasanuddin.

In short: your data stays on your own device (browser or phone), there is no Sulo server, no analytics, ads or tracking, and nothing is sent to the developer or to third parties. Sulo only reads SIKOLA, never changes anything there, and never asks for your password.

Browser extension (Chrome and Edge) · Android app

Browser extension (Chrome and Edge)

What Sulo reads

Sulo uses the SIKOLA session that already exists in your browser to read your own data:

  • your list of courses
  • assignments and their due dates, including quiz deadlines
  • the structure of each active course (sections and activities), a few times a day, to spot new materials and tasks
  • your 20 latest SIKOLA notifications, to spot new grades, feedback and forum posts

Sulo only reads. It never submits work, never marks anything as read, never changes data in SIKOLA, never reads quiz content, and never reads other students' data.

What Sulo stores, and where

Everything is stored locally in your browser (chrome.storage) on your own device:

  • courses, assignments and due dates
  • your attendance recap from SIKOLA, updated automatically at most once a day, and the per-session details, fetched only when you open them (for the courses you follow: sessions recorded, points, percentage, status, and remarks)
  • the last seen structure of each course and the "Latest updates" log (at most 200 entries)
  • your choices: the courses you follow, tasks marked done, course display names and colors, and a nickname you type yourself
  • a technical log of the last 300 checks of SIKOLA: only the time, the function names and the status, with no content; never sent, and only included when you copy "info for a bug report" yourself
  • local usage counters, which never leave your device unless you export them yourself

From SIKOLA notifications, Sulo keeps only the id, the subject, the component and event type, when it was created, whether it has been read, the related page address (known SIKOLA pages only, with no parameters other than ids) and the course number. Message bodies (text, fullmessage, fullmessagehtml, smallmessage) and extra data (customdata), which may contain grades or lecturer comments, are dropped when read and never stored. Sulo's own notifications about grades never mention the grade or the comment.

Local usage statistics (how often the popup and dashboard were opened, tasks marked as done and reminders shown) are numbers only and stay in your browser. Sulo never sends them. They are not shown and cannot be exported in the regular version; only development builds show them.

Data is tied to your SIKOLA account, recognised by your SIKOLA user number (userid), stored as is in your browser. If a different account signs in to SIKOLA on the same browser, the previous account's data is hidden at once and Sulo stops checking and reminding. That data is deleted only after you choose "Use this account", or when you use "Delete all data". If you sign in with the previous account again, everything comes back.

What Sulo never does

  • Never asks for, reads or stores your username or password.
  • Never stores cookies, session keys or tokens beyond the current browser session.
  • Never sends your data to the developer, to a server, or to any third party.
  • No analytics, no telemetry, no advertising.
  • No automation of academic tasks: Sulo does not fill in course registration, surveys or attendance.

Network requests

Sulo makes requests to two places only:

  1. SIKOLA (sikola-v2.unhas.ac.id), to read your own data. At most 40 requests per day (typically 5 to 10), one at a time, not during quiet hours (00.00 to 06.00), and not while your computer is idle.
  2. Sulo's public data repository on GitHub Pages (ikrar06.github.io/sulo-data), to fetch a small configuration file and the academic calendar data. These requests carry no information about you (no cookies, extra headers or parameters) and are made at most once a day per file. As with any website, GitHub can see your IP address when a file is fetched.

"Add to Google Calendar" in the task menu only opens a Google Calendar page in a new tab when you click it. That page is prefilled with the task name, course name, due time and a link to the task on SIKOLA. Sulo itself sends nothing to Google and needs no login; you decide whether to save it in Google Calendar.

The "Buy me a coffee" button (Trakteer), social media links and "Send feedback" (Google Form) on the About page, and the link to the official calendar PDF, only open that site in a new tab when you click them. Until you click, Sulo does not contact that site at all, and no script, image or font from it is loaded into Sulo's pages. Sulo sends no data there and never fills in a form for you.

NEOSIA module (optional)

Off by default. If you turn on "Connect NEOSIA" in Settings, Sulo first shows a consent screen with the text below, then Chrome asks for its permission.

Sulo only reads data while you open NEOSIA yourself. Sulo never contacts NEOSIA.

What is kept in your browser

  • Class schedule: courses, classes, days, times, rooms and lecturer names
  • The KRS window and status, and your credit limit
  • Paid or not paid, without amounts
  • The survey status: filled in or not
  • Letter grades, semester and overall GPA, and credits. Hidden until you choose Show
  • Your semester and study period
  • Your academic advisor’s name

What is dropped before it leaves the NEOSIA page

  • Student number, national ID and school ID numbers
  • Contact details: email and phone number
  • Address and date of birth
  • Payment amounts and bank
  • Numeric grades
  • Lecturers’ NIP, NIDN and NUPTK numbers

Turning it off

Any time, in Settings with "Disconnect and delete data". All NEOSIA data is deleted and the permission is removed.

  • Its permissions are optional: "scripting" and access to the neosia.unhas.ac.id pages. Both are asked for only when you turn the module on, and removed when it is turned off. Sulo does not ask for access to the NEOSIA API address. If you remove one in Chrome's settings, the module turns itself off and its data is deleted.
  • Sulo never sends a request to NEOSIA. Two small scripts on NEOSIA pages read the responses the NEOSIA app already asked for, pick out the fields that may be kept right there on the page, and drop the rest. The full responses are never stored, logged or sent.
  • The survey link, your personal data page in NEOSIA and the withdrawal page are never read. The NEOSIA login token is never read.
  • Grades and GPA never appear in notifications, exports, copied lists, calendar files or bug report info. A new-grade notification names the course only.
  • Privacy mode (in Settings, or the eye icon in the dashboard) masks names, grades, GPA and credits on screen.
  • No automation: Sulo never fills in KRS, surveys or attendance, and never watches class capacity.

Deleting your data

  • Removing the extension from your browser deletes all of its data. This works today.
  • "Delete all data" in Settings (under "Delete data") deletes everything Sulo keeps in this browser (tasks, courses, reminders, latest updates and settings) without removing the extension. Nothing in SIKOLA is touched.
  • "Disconnect and delete data" on the NEOSIA card (Settings) deletes all NEOSIA data and removes its permissions. "Delete all data" also turns the NEOSIA module off.

Android app

What is stored

  • Tasks and deadlines from SIKOLA, and the notes, steps and personal deadlines you add yourself.
  • Your course list, including the names and colors you choose.
  • Course structures for Updates (activity names and kinds, not their content).
  • The attendance recap for the courses you follow, and the per-session details you open.
  • Your settings, and the SIKOLA sign-in session.

Never stored or read: your SIKOLA password, quiz content, and other students’ data.

Data is tied to your SIKOLA account. When another account signs in, the previous account’s data is hidden at once and Sulo stops checking and reminding, background watching included. That data, its NEOSIA data too, is deleted only after you choose "Use this account".

Where it is stored

Everything is in the app’s private storage on this phone, which other apps cannot read. Android backup and transfer to another phone are turned off for Sulo, so the data never goes into a cloud backup.

Encryption

  • The SIKOLA sign-in session is encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Its key lives in the Android Keystore and cannot leave the phone.
  • The session never reaches the app’s interface code, never goes into a log, and is never part of the bug report info.
  • The optional app lock asks for your fingerprint or the phone’s screen lock whenever Sulo opens.
  • Sulo’s data can only be opened after the phone has been unlocked once since it was turned on. If the session key is lost or can no longer be used, the unreadable session is deleted and Sulo asks you to sign in again.

Servers the app contacts

  • sikola-v2.unhas.ac.id: you sign in on SIKOLA’s own page, then Sulo reads tasks, the calendar, courses, updates and attendance. Read only; Sulo changes nothing on SIKOLA. Requests name themselves as Sulo and its version.
  • ikrar06.github.io: Sulo’s public data repository, for two data files only: the remote settings (including whether the maintainer has turned watching off) and the latest academic calendar. The calendar is read at most once a day, plus when you open the app and the last read is over 6 hours old. The remote settings are read at most every 6 hours, by the app when you open it or by background watching if it is on. The request carries no cookie and nothing that identifies you.
  • neosia.unhas.ac.id (only if you connect NEOSIA): NEOSIA’s pages open inside Sulo only when you tap them, and those pages load their own data. Sulo never sends a request to NEOSIA.
  • The same remote settings also tell you when a new Sulo version is out. Download opens the release page on github.com in your browser; Sulo never downloads or installs anything itself. For a security fix, an old version can be asked to update first: until then Sulo does not check SIKOLA, and your data stays.
  • No other server. No Sulo server, analytics, ads or tracking. The academic calendar also ships inside the app, so it is there without a connection.
  • Links you tap (Google Calendar, SIKOLA, the feedback form) open in your browser. Sulo sends nothing to them.

When Sulo checks SIKOLA

Because of something you do: after signing in, when you open the app and the data is older than 15 minutes, pull to update, or the Update button. Plus background watching if you turn it on (next section). The attendance recap updates at most once a day when the app is opened, never in the background; per-session details are fetched when you open them. Reminders are scheduled on the phone from the latest data.

Background watching (optional)

  • With "Watch for new tasks" on, Sulo checks SIKOLA regularly even when the app is closed: about every 20 minutes from 06.00 to 22.59 and every 110 minutes at night. Each check is one request that only reads tasks, updates and the session’s time left.
  • While it is on, your SIKOLA sign-in stays active on this phone, because SIKOLA counts the checks as activity. Turn it off if you do not want your session kept active.
  • To turn it off: More, Settings, Notifications, "Watch for new tasks". Checks stop at once; after that Sulo only checks when you open the app, pull down, or tap Update.
  • Sulo’s maintainer can turn watching off or slow it down for everyone through the remote settings, for example if the university objects. Watching reads those settings itself at most every 6 hours, so a change applies without you opening the app. If the settings cannot be read for 72 hours, watching stops checking SIKOLA until they can.
  • If you do not open Sulo for 7 days, watching stops with one notification. Open Sulo to resume it.
  • The checks count against the same daily limits as every other check, and never fetch the attendance recap.

NEOSIA (optional)

  • Off until you connect it. You sign in on NEOSIA’s own page; Sulo reads neither your password nor NEOSIA’s sign-in token, and the sign-in page never gets Sulo’s script.
  • From the pages you open, Sulo keeps the class schedule, classes, KRS status, your advisor’s name, payment status (paid or not), letter grades, semester and cumulative GPA, credits, study period, the KRS window and the survey status. Student number, ID number, address, birth date, contacts, numeric scores and payment amounts are dropped before anything is stored. The survey link is never read.
  • All NEOSIA data is stored encrypted with an Android Keystore key of its own, apart from the SIKOLA session. Grades and GPA are hidden by default, opened only while the Grades screen or the Studi card shows them, and never go into notifications, exports or the bug report info.
  • While grades or the GPA are on screen, other apps cannot record or capture Sulo’s screen, and its preview in the recent-apps list is blank.

How to delete it

  • More, Settings, Sign out and delete data: deletes the session, its Keystore key, all of Sulo’s data and every scheduled reminder on this phone.
  • More, Settings, NEOSIA, Disconnect NEOSIA: deletes all NEOSIA data and the NEOSIA sign-in on this phone. Signing out deletes it too.
  • Uninstalling the app deletes everything too.
  • Nothing on SIKOLA or NEOSIA changes.

Changes to this policy

Changes are published with new versions of Sulo, and the date at the top is updated. If the privacy notice shown during setup changes, Sulo shows it again.

Contact

Questions about privacy can be sent through the feedback form: https://forms.gle/XsBuWXGHNR4pPTs17. Please do not include your student number, password, grades or other personal data in your message.
